items.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: There was Shadow Wilson, I don’t know if you remember, they were in line to see us.

ctx.x: Yeah. “Flyin’ Home,” “Body and Soul,” these were the things that were happening at that time. “Satin Doll” was still there and “A Train.” All the things that they’re even doing

nowadays. And “C Jam Blues.” All those tunes, we used to — the place would be packed. Like I told you we had to break into — Lester Young was in line. There was Shadow Wilson, I don’t know if you remember, they were in line to see us. Around the corner was the Howard Theater, where all the big bands used to come play, and they’d come in and see us. And we had a cooking group. And the reason it broke up, we were there 17 weeks, six nights a week for five hours a night playing hard, I mean playing hard. And the…
This club in Washington where you had these 17 weeks, you had a racially mixed band, was it any problem with that?
